data.topic: portable per-project AI decision memory: vector-backed decision tracking for legacy codebases that auto-discovers implicit architectural decisions, stores them with file-level associations in a portable embedded database, and dynamically injects relevant context at edit time

synthesized_findings.theme: Portable vector storage: sqlite-vec + embedded embeddings

claims.claim: sqlite-vec is the modern zero-dependency C successor to sqlite-vss, replacing Faiss/C++ with pure C. Works on macOS, Linux, Windows, WASM, Android, iOS. Installs via pip install sqlite-vec.

sqlite-vec queries 100k float vectors at 768d in <75ms on disk. At 256d, well under 50ms. Binary quantization drops 100k queries to ~11ms with ~95% accuracy retention. Practical float ceiling is ~300-500k vectors before breaching 100ms.

A pre-built SQLite .db file with embeddings stored as BLOBs in sqlite-vec shadow tables is fully portable across machines — the embedding data travels with the file. Querying requires either re-running an embedding model on the query string or using keyword fallback via FTS5.
FastEmbed (by Qdrant) uses ONNX Runtime for local embedding without Ollama — no GPU, no CUDA, no server. pip install fastembed. ~15ms/chunk on CPU. Models download on first use, then fully offline.
nomic-embed-text-v1.5 supports ONNX export for serverless inference via onnxruntime (Python) and Transformers.js (Node). Supports Matryoshka embeddings with 8192-token context window.

Hybrid BM25 + vector search via SQLite FTS5 + sqlite-vec with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) is a documented working pattern. If embedding model is unavailable, keyword search still works from the same SQLite file.

synthesized_findings.key_insight: The full portability stack exists: sqlite-vec (zero-dep vector store) + FastEmbed/ONNX (serverless embedding) + FTS5 BM25 fallback (no-model keyword search). A single .db file is portable; querying is portable via ONNX or degrades gracefully to keyword search.

claims.claim: nomic-embed-text-v1.5 MTEB scores by dimension: 768→62.28, 512→61.96, 256→61.04, 128→59.34, 64→56.10. Truncating from 768 to 256 costs only ~1.2% retrieval quality while halving storage and improving query speed.

To truncate Matryoshka embeddings: apply layer normalization, slice to target dimension, then L2 normalize. Requires task prefixes for code: 'search_document: <code>' for indexing, 'search_query: <query>' for retrieval.
For a 100k-function codebase at 256d float32, total embedding storage is ~100MB. At 768d, ~300MB. Both within sqlite-vec's operational range.

synthesized_findings.key_insight: 256-dimensional nomic-embed-text-v1.5 is the pragmatic sweet spot for decision memory: 98.8% of full-dimension quality, ~100MB for 100k functions, sub-50ms sqlite-vec queries. No reason to use 768d unless top-1 precision is critical.

synthesized_findings.theme: Auto-discovery of implicit architectural decisions — research gap

claims.claim: A 2025 systematic literature review of 18 papers confirms LLMs are applied to design decision classification and pattern detection, but current approaches mostly use simple prompting. No published system extracts implicit/unannotated decisions from code behavior.

Self-Admitted Technical Debt (SATD) detection using transformer models achieves F1 ~0.76 on explicitly annotated debt in comments/commits. It does NOT address implicit workarounds or load-bearing hacks without developer annotations.

GPT-4 achieves 0.849 BERTScore F1 generating architectural design decisions from provided contexts in zero-shot mode — but this generates decisions FROM contexts, not extracting/recovering implicit decisions from code.
NLP-based SATD detection pipelines produce 44% false positives or context-insufficient instances, requiring human validation to separate signal from noise.
LLMs struggle specifically with complex abstractions and class relationships in architecture recovery — precisely where implicit load-bearing decisions tend to live.

synthesized_findings.key_insight: Auto-discovery of implicit decisions is genuinely novel — no published system does it. The closest path is a multi-stage pipeline: SATD comment detection + commit classification + LLM-based rationale synthesis. But this pipeline has NOT been evaluated as a unified system. Expect 44% false positive rate requiring human-in-the-loop validation.

synthesized_findings.theme: Per-project AI memory: state of the art

claims.claim: Cursor uses remote Turbopuffer vector DB with Merkle tree per-project isolation. Indexing reuse cut 99th percentile from 4.03 hours to 21 seconds by caching embeddings per chunk content hash.

Continue.dev uses locally embedded LanceDB with SQL-filtered retrieval. ~10-line code chunks, ~1M vectors for 10M-line codebase, sub-10ms query latency, SQL-like filtering by language/project/tags. 40% relevance improvement reported.
Windsurf Cascade separates auto-generated 'Memories' (dynamic facts/decisions) from '.windsurf/rules' (static standards). Storage format undocumented.

Mem0 open source uses three-tier storage: Qdrant (vector), Neo4j/Memgraph (graph relationships), SQLite (history). Research reports 26% LLM-as-Judge improvement, 91% lower p95 latency, 90% token cost reduction vs full-context.

No cross-tool portability standard exists — no way to move learned project memories from Cursor to Windsurf or vice versa. Per-project AI memory stores as standalone libraries are nascent outside IDE-embedded solutions.

synthesized_findings.key_insight: All major tools have vector-backed per-project indexes, but they're proprietary and non-portable. Continue.dev + LanceDB is the most transparent architecture. A tool-agnostic portable decision store that works across Claude Code, Cursor, and others would fill a real gap.

synthesized_findings.theme: Edit-time context injection: no one does it automatically

claims.claim: No major AI coding tool (Cursor, Continue, Copilot) natively auto-injects context on file open or modification. All mechanisms are query-triggered (@Codebase), user-triggered (@ dropdown), or rule/glob-scoped (Claude Code Rules).

Claude Code path-glob Rules are the closest existing primitive: they load context when a file matching a glob pattern becomes active. Combined with Hooks (lifecycle callbacks on file edits), this is the most composable foundation for building edit-time injection.
MCP dynamic-context-mcp injects rules based on file-path glob patterns. MCP supports dynamic tool registration at runtime — file-open events could trigger context server updates.
GitHub Copilot uses Jaccard similarity on open tabs and recent history for fast-path context. Cursor uses Merkle tree + Tree-sitter syntactic chunking for semantic completeness.
Continue.dev has an open GitHub issue requesting automatic local/IDE context injection, confirming this is not yet a native feature anywhere.

synthesized_findings.key_insight: Edit-time auto-injection of decisions is novel. The implementation path is an MCP server that accepts file paths, queries the project decision DB, and returns relevant decisions — triggered by Claude Code hooks or glob-matched rules. No existing tool does this.

claims.claim: AST-based function-level chunking (tree-sitter, depth-first traversal, merge siblings under token limit) outperforms fixed-size chunking: +4.3 Recall@5 on RepoEval, +2.67 Pass@1 on SWE-bench.
Class-aware semantic chunking (prepending class signatures to method bodies) significantly reduces hallucination vs naive per-function or fixed-size chunking.
Content-hash incremental indexing (SHA-256 per chunk, Merkle tree change detection) prevents redundant embedding. Cursor runs this every 10 minutes, re-indexing only changed files.
Binary quantization of embeddings (float32 to 1-bit) retains ~95% accuracy while reducing storage 32x and query time ~10x in sqlite-vec.

synthesized_findings.key_insight: Function-level AST chunking + content-hash incremental re-indexing is the proven approach. For decisions specifically (not code chunks), the unit of embedding is the decision text + associated file paths — much simpler than code chunking.

angle_summaries.angle: Portable vector stores without runtime dependencies
key_insights: sqlite-vec + FastEmbed/ONNX = fully portable vector search without Ollama
Hybrid FTS5 + sqlite-vec with RRF provides graceful degradation
Single .db file is self-contained and cross-platform
Confirmed research gap — no system extracts implicit decisions from code
SATD detection handles explicit debt only, 44% false positive rate
Multi-stage pipeline (SATD + commits + LLM synthesis) is untested as unified system

angle_summaries.angle: Per-project AI memory systems beyond flat files
key_insights: All major tools have vector indexes but proprietary and non-portable
Continue.dev + LanceDB is most transparent open-source reference

angle_summaries.angle: Edit-time context injection for AI coding tools
key_insights: No tool auto-injects context at edit time — all are query/user-triggered
Claude Code glob rules + hooks are the closest foundation
MCP servers are the right extension point for custom injection

angle_summaries.angle: Embedding strategies and scaling for 100k+ LOC
key_insights: 100k LOC maps to ~3-10k function chunks, sqlite-vec handles in <20ms
256d Matryoshka is the sweet spot — 98.8% quality, half the storage
Content-hash incremental indexing skips 99% of work on typical commits

conflicts.topic: Refactor Simulation as an emerging technique for detecting load-bearing code

gemini_claim.claim: Refactor Simulation is an emerging technique where an LLM is prompted to simulate a fix for suspected hacks to identify hidden dependencies and regressions

claude_claim.claim: No published technique was found specifically targeting refactor simulation or code smell inversion to detect intentional workarounds. The arxiv ID may be synthetic.

conflicts.credibility_assessment: Gemini's arxiv URLs for this specific claim look synthetic (round numbers, no matching paper found by Claude's web search). The concept is plausible but unverified. Treat as speculative — do not build on this without confirming the source.

gaps: No published end-to-end system for extracting implicit architectural decisions from code behavior (confirmed research gap)
Nomic-embed-text ONNX weights availability — unclear if Nomic publishes official ONNX exports or if conversion is DIY
Matryoshka dimension impact specifically on code retrieval (vs general MTEB) — not benchmarked separately
sqlite-lembed (in-process GGUF embedding extension) production stability unclear — may be demo-quality only
Cross-platform binary management for sqlite-vec on exotic architectures beyond standard pip/npm
Windsurf Cascade internal storage format for Memories undocumented
Specific internal context weighting algorithms (recently-edited vs semantically-similar) remain proprietary across all tools
No public benchmark combining nomic-embed-text-v1.5 + sqlite-vec end-to-end on a real 100k+ LOC codebase
